_doc: Plot Twists (R. Talsorian, Cyberpunk RED: Single Player Mode, SPM p.75-76: a d100 table, 50 rows of 2 points each; the Mission Builder's step 5, SPM p.28: near the job's completion, only when the story wants one, not on every job). Read by Twist (src/tactical/twist.gd): MissionBuilder.twist rolls one onto a board offer, hidden (gig.twist {row, id, label, trigger}); the encounter springs it at its trigger and applies its fx. The roll positions are the book's; every label and note is our own short paraphrase. A row plays only when it has no `unmodelled` and every fx key is one Twist implements (tests/unit/tactical/test_twists.gd); the others keep the fx they would need, for later. `objectives`: the gig objectives a row fits (absent: any); a twist rolled onto a gig it doesn't fit is rolled again, as the Mission Types step does.

chance._why: HOUSE-RULE (owner: not every gig has a twist; aim for 1 in 4 to 1 in 3). Whether an offer gets one is a Closed Question to the Oracle (SPM p.12-13), 'Does this job take a turn?', at a likelihood by the gig's 1-3 security level, and only the plain yes answer gives one (yes with a complication would put a twist on 35% of street jobs). Unlikely's yes is 25% (rolls 76-100), 50/50's 40% (61-100): a fortress's job goes sideways more often.

triggers._why: When a twist springs (HOUSE-RULE readings of 'near completion, or earlier', SPM p.28). objective_done: the objective's main part is done and only getting out is left (Objective.near_done); `or_round`: it springs at that round anyway. round: at the start of round n (a [lo, hi] range is rolled when the offer is made). alarm: when the alarm goes up (backup called). start: as the gig starts (for what the engine can only place before the map is drawn).
